title: Messaging Slack Notified Event
description: A Slack alert that is not itself a received message: a mention, a reaction, or an activity ping. One type per platform (messaging.<platform>.notified); a new message is messaging.slack.received, never this. ordering_key is messaging:slack:<thread_id> when the alert belongs to a thread (so it orders with that thread's messages), else messaging:slack:<notification_id>. Consumers deduplicate on notification_id. See bloodbank/docs/event-naming.md (messaging).

ordering_key.description: Section 11.1 bucket 'messaging:slack:<thread_id>' when data.thread_id is present, else 'messaging:slack:<notification_id>'.

category.description: What kind of alert: mention (someone addressed the operator), reaction (someone reacted to a message), activity (any other platform ping).

handle.description: Platform address of whoever triggered the notification.

display_name.description: Their display name, when the platform exposes one.

sender.description: Who triggered the notification (the person who mentioned or reacted), when there is one. Absent for platform/system activity pings.

handle.description: Platform address of the notified account.

display_name.description: Display name of the notified account, when the platform exposes one.

recipient.description: Who the notification was delivered to, in platform terms.

summary.description: The alert text as the platform presents it. May be truncated.

reaction.description: The reaction (emoji or platform reaction name) when category is reaction.

received_at.description: When the platform raised the alert (source clock), RFC 3339.

notification_id.description: Platform-native (or producer-derived, stable) alert ID; consumers deduplicate on it.

thread_id.description: Platform-native thread/chat ID the alert belongs to, when it belongs to one; names the ordering bucket.

message_id.description: The message the alert is about (the mentioning or reacted-to message), when there is one; joins to messaging.slack.received data.message_id.
